requirement: The getting-started documentation MUST show users how to install and initialize Symposium, add `habeas` as a project dev dependency, enable its plugin with `cargo agents use habeas`, and then configure the project with the globally installed `habeas setup` command. It MUST explain how to refresh skills with `cargo agents sync` and how to preserve local edits when moving from skills copied by older Habeas versions.
rationale: The getting-started guide shows Symposium installation and initialization, adds Habeas as a dev dependency, enables the plugin, and then runs the globally installed CLI for setup. It documents the separate cargo install habeas step currently required by Symposium 0.5.1, plus skill refresh and preservation of local edits during migration.

text: Start with a Cargo project that already has an mdBook (`book.toml` and a `SUMMARY.md` in the book source directory).
Install [Symposium](https://github.com/symposium-dev/symposium) and select your agents once on this machine:
From the project directory, add Habeas and enable its Symposium plugin:
Symposium 0.5.1 does not yet install the CLI when enabling Habeas's plugin. Until that works, install it separately and configure the project:

`habeas setup` adds Habeas as a Cargo dev dependency, configures mdBook to use the installed `habeas mdbook` preprocessor, copies the badge stylesheet, and creates `tests/habeas.rs`. That test calls `habeas::validate()`, so normal Cargo tests check your requirements and evidence.

`cargo agents use habeas` enables the plugin for this workspace and syncs Habeas's skills into your configured agents. Run `cargo agents sync` after updating the Habeas dependency to refresh the skills. Use `cargo agents use habeas --global` if you want the plugin enabled in every workspace; the crate still needs to be a dependency for its skills to apply.

If you previously ran `habeas agents` or `habeas setup --install-skills`, inspect the resulting `.agents/skills/habeas-*` directories for local edits before your first Symposium sync. Save customized files under different names or elsewhere, remove those old copies, and run `cargo agents sync` to receive Symposium-managed skills.
Install Symposium and select the agents you use:
Run these commands from a Cargo project that already has `book.toml` and a mdBook `SUMMARY.md`:
The separate `cargo install habeas` step is needed with Symposium 0.5.1, which does not yet install the CLI when enabling the plugin. For development from a checkout, use `cargo install --path .`.

`habeas setup` adds Habeas as a dev dependency, configures `[preprocessor.habeas]` to run `habeas mdbook`, adds the badge stylesheet, and creates `tests/habeas.rs`. Setup can be run again without duplicating configuration or overwriting differing files.

`cargo agents use habeas` enables Habeas's Symposium plugin and syncs the bundled skills from the selected Habeas crate version. Run `cargo agents sync` after updating the dependency to refresh the skills.

If Habeas previously copied skills into `.agents/skills/habeas-*`, review them for local edits before the first Symposium sync. Save any edits under different names or elsewhere, remove those old copies, and then sync so Symposium can manage them.
